summary: The Teufelberger drenaLINE Climbing Line is a climbing line for tree climbing on a hitch or device. Here is how it handles on the job, what to check before you buy, and how to keep it in service.
highlights: Holds its round shape under a hitch
Runs smoothly through pulleys and devices
Bright colors easy to track in the canopy
specs: Red, white and blue (Stars and Stripes pattern)

p: drenaLINE is one of Teufelberger's best-known arborist lines, and the Stars and Stripes version is the same rope in a red, white and blue pattern. Climbers pick it for a firm, round braid that keeps its shape under load and a cover that bites cleanly in a friction hitch.

A 24-strand cover is tightly braided and round, so the rope holds its shape under a hitch, feeds smoothly through pulleys and mechanical devices, and resists flattening over branch unions. Lines like this are used for moving rope (MRS/DdRT) climbing and, where the manufacturer lists the rope as compatible, for stationary rope (SRS) work. Most climbers buy them in hanks with a spliced eye on one end.

Before you buy, check the diameter range of your hitch cord, ascenders and descent device, since compatibility is set by those makers. You can compare it with the other 24-strand climbing ropes we carry.

Climbing rope is life-support equipment. It must meet the applicable standard, ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Inspect it before every climb for cuts, glazing, sheath damage and soft or stiff spots, keep it away from saws, fuel and bar oil, and retire it when in doubt. Get trained before you climb.

faq.q: Can I use Teufelberger drenaLINE Climbing Line for SRS as well as MRS?
faq.a: Many 24-strand lines work for both, but device compatibility is set by the device maker. Check that your SRS device is approved for this rope and its diameter before you climb on it.

faq.q: What hitch cord works with Teufelberger drenaLINE Climbing Line?
faq.a: Hitch cord should be smaller in diameter than the climbing line and tested on it before use. Tie the hitch, load it on the ground, and make sure it grabs and releases the way you expect.

name: Yale KernMaster Static Rope, Blue and Orange, 11mm
title: Yale KernMaster Static Rope, Blue and Orange, 11mm
h1: Yale KernMaster Static Rope, Blue and Orange, 11mm
meta: Yale KernMaster Static Rope, Blue and Orange, 11mm for SRS climbing and access lines. What it is, how it handles, sizing and care, plus the typical price.
tagline: Yale Cordage low-stretch static rope for SRS climbing and access lines.
summary: The Yale KernMaster Static Rope is a low-stretch static rope for SRS climbing and access lines. Here is how it handles on the job, what to check before you buy, and how to keep it in service.
highlights: Good for access lines and fixed lines
specs: SRS climbing, access and fixed lines

p: KernMaster is Yale's 11 mm kernmantle static rope, here in blue and orange. A sheath-and-core rope like this stretches very little, which is exactly what you want when you are ascending a single rope and do not want to bounce out every bit of stretch before you gain height.

In a static kernmantle rope the core carries most of the load and the sheath protects it from abrasion. Because it stretches very little, more of each stroke on an ascent turns into height, which is why low-stretch rope is common for SRS climbing and access lines. The flip side is that it absorbs little energy, so it is not meant to catch a fall with slack in the system.

Before you buy, check the diameter range of your hitch cord, ascenders and descent device, since compatibility is set by those makers. You can compare it with the other 24-strand climbing ropes we carry.

Climbing rope is life-support equipment. It must meet the applicable standard, ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions. Inspect it before every climb for cuts, glazing, sheath damage and soft or stiff spots, keep it away from saws, fuel and bar oil, and retire it when in doubt. Get trained before you climb.

faq.q: Is Yale KernMaster Static Rope good for SRS?
faq.a: Low-stretch kernmantle rope is a common SRS choice because ascents are more efficient. Confirm that your ascenders and descent device are approved for this rope and diameter.

faq.q: Can I tie a friction hitch on Yale KernMaster Static Rope?
faq.a: Some static ropes work well with hitches and some do not. Test any hitch cord on the rope on the ground before climbing, and follow the rope and device manufacturers' guidance.

body.h: Where this rope fits in a rigging system
p: Atlas is Sterling's arborist rigging line, and the 1/2 in size is the light end of the range. It is easy to carry, easy to throw over a limb and quick to tie, which makes it a good fit for pruning cuts, lowering small limbs and light removal work.

Rigging rope takes repeated shock loads, runs through blocks and lowering devices, and gets dragged over bark and brush all day. Match the diameter to the wood you are taking down and to the rest of the system: blocks, slings and the lowering device all need to be rated for the same rope and the forces involved. Dynamic loads from a dropped piece can be several times its weight, so leave plenty of margin.

Pick the diameter for the biggest wood you plan to rig, not the average piece, and make sure your lowering device and blocks are rated for it. If you need another size, compare the other rigging ropes we carry.

Inspect the rope before every job for cuts, glazing, pulled strands and core damage, and keep it clean and out of saw chips and bar oil. Rig within the rated strength of every component, and make sure the crew is trained in rigging practice under ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions.

faq.q: How do I pick a rigging rope size?
faq.a: Size the rope to the heaviest pieces you plan to lower, then match blocks, slings and the lowering device to that rope. When in doubt, step up a size or take smaller pieces.

faq.q: How long does Sterling Atlas 1/2 last?
faq.a: It depends on loads, abrasion and care. Retire rigging rope that shows glazing, cut strands, core damage or stiff, flattened sections, and track its use.

name: Samson Tenex-TEC Rope by the Foot
title: Samson Tenex-TEC Rope by the Foot: Specs & Buying Guide
h1: Samson Tenex-TEC Rope by the Foot
meta: Samson Tenex-TEC Rope by the Foot for splicing slings, loopies and tails. What it is, how it handles, sizing and care, plus the typical price.
tagline: Samson Rope splicing rope for splicing slings, loopies and tails.
summary: The Samson Tenex-TEC is a splicing rope for splicing slings, loopies and tails. Sold by the foot so you can cut exactly the length you need. Here is how it handles on the job, what to check before you buy, and how to keep it in service.
highlights: Sold by the foot, cut to your length
Easy to splice for slings and loopies

p: Tenex-TEC is a heat-treated version of Samson's 12-strand polyester Tenex, made to be firmer and stretch less than standard Tenex. Buying it by the foot lets you cut exactly what you need for spliced slings, loopies and adjustable tails.

A 12-strand single braid is hollow, which makes it quick to splice: bury a tail, lock-stitch if the instructions call for it, and you have a clean eye without hardware. Polyester holds up well to sunlight and abrasion and stretches less than nylon, and a firm single braid keeps its shape in a sling or tail that gets clipped, loaded and unloaded all day. Only splice life-support items if you have been trained to do it, and follow the manufacturer's splicing instructions.
Size the rope to the hardware and the job: thinner cord for loopies and friction saver tails, heavier rope for slings that take rigging loads. See the other rigging ropes for complete lines.

Inspect spliced items before each use for pulled strands, fuzzing at the bury and glazing. Anything used for life support must meet ANSI Z133 and the manufacturer's instructions, be inspected regularly, and be made and used by trained people.

faq.q: Can I splice Samson Tenex-TEC myself?
faq.a: Yes, a 12-strand single braid is one of the easier ropes to splice, but use the manufacturer's instructions and get trained before splicing anything used for life support.

faq.q: Why buy Samson Tenex-TEC by the foot?
faq.a: You pay only for the length you need for a sling, loopie or tail, and you can cut several projects from one order.
